authorities.locator: Section 1651(a), preliminary edition current through July 29, 2026
authorities.proposition: The Supreme Court and all courts established by Act of Congress may issue writs necessary or appropriate in aid of their respective jurisdictions and agreeable to the usages and principles of law.

authorities.locator: Section 3730(h), preliminary edition current through July 29, 2026
authorities.proposition: Section 3730(h) supplies only the fictional federal-question background for Calder's retaliation complaint. The Cinder Lake writ materials make no conclusion about the merits of that statutory claim.

authorities.locator: Rule 501 in the official compilation effective December 1, 2025, PDF page 23
authorities.proposition: Federal common law governs privilege unless the Constitution, a federal statute, or Supreme Court rules provide otherwise; state law governs privilege only as to a claim or defense for which state law supplies the rule of decision.

authorities.locator: Rule 502(a) and (d) in the official compilation effective December 1, 2025, PDF pages 23-24
authorities.proposition: An intentional disclosure in a federal proceeding or to a federal office or agency extends waiver to an undisclosed communication or information only when it concerns the same subject matter and fairness requires considering both together. A federal court may order that a litigation disclosure does not waive privilege or protection in any other federal or state proceeding.

authorities.locator: Rules 26(b)(3), 26(b)(5), 26(c), and 26(f) in the official compilation effective December 1, 2025, PDF pages 59-67
authorities.proposition: Rule 26 protects qualifying trial-preparation material, requires an express privilege claim with a sufficient description, provides sequestration and resolution procedures after notice of produced privileged material, authorizes protective orders for good cause after conferral, and requires discovery planning to address privilege-claim procedures and possible Rule 502 orders.

authorities.locator: Rule 37(a)(1) and (a)(3) in the official compilation effective December 1, 2025, PDF pages 79-80
authorities.proposition: A motion to compel must certify a good-faith conference or attempted conference, and a party may seek an order compelling disclosure or discovery for the failures identified by Rule 37(a)(3).

authorities.citation: Upjohn Co. v. United States, 449 U.S. 383, 389–97 (1981)
authorities.proposition: The corporate attorney-client privilege protects confidential employee communications made at superiors' direction to corporate counsel for legal advice when the employees know that purpose. It protects communications, not the underlying facts, and does not prevent discovery of facts from their original sources.

authorities.citation: Cheney v. U.S. District Court, 542 U.S. 367, 380–81 (2004)
authorities.proposition: Mandamus requires that the petitioner have no other adequate means to obtain relief, show a clear and indisputable right, and persuade the issuing court that the writ is appropriate under the circumstances.

authorities.citation: Mohawk Industries, Inc. v. Carpenter, 558 U.S. 100, 108–11 (2009)
authorities.proposition: Disclosure orders adverse to the attorney-client privilege do not qualify for collateral-order appeal. Postjudgment review and other mechanisms ordinarily suffice, while mandamus remains available only in extraordinary circumstances involving a judicial-usurpation or clear-abuse concern.

authorities.citation: In re Murphy-Brown, LLC, 907 F.3d 788, 795–97 (4th Cir. 2018)
authorities.locator: No. 18-1762, official published slip opinion pages 9-13
authorities.proposition: The Fourth Circuit applies Cheney's three conditions strictly but may issue mandamus when ordinary appellate review cannot supply adequate relief, the asserted right is clear and indisputable, and the writ is appropriate in the court's discretion.

authorities.citation: Sky Angel U.S., LLC v. Discovery Communications, LLC, 885 F.3d 271, 276–77 (4th Cir. 2018)
authorities.locator: No. 16-2050, official published slip opinion pages 6-7
authorities.proposition: Rule 502(a) subject-matter waiver begins with an intentional disclosure of privileged or protected communication or information. Revealing a conclusion, acting on advice, or creating an inference that advice was received does not by itself disclose the privileged communication.

authorities.locator: No. 97-1684, official published slip opinion pages 4-8
authorities.proposition: The privilege proponent bears the burden of establishing confidential attorney-client communications, and voluntary actual disclosure can waive protection. Because Hawkins predates Rule 502, it does not supply a categorical modern subject-matter-waiver rule.

authorities.citation: In re Fluor Intercontinental, Inc., No. 20-1241, 2020 WL 1472076 (4th Cir. Mar. 25, 2020) (unpublished)
authorities.proposition: In a nonprecedential and narrowly analogous disposition, the Fourth Circuit granted mandamus from a seven-day privilege-production order because a disclosure of conclusions and general subject matter did not reveal privileged communications and did not support categorical waiver. The Cinder Lake materials do not treat Fluor as binding or extend it beyond that exact persuasive analogy.

authorities.locator: Official May 2023 Local Civil Rules, Rule 7.1(c), (f)(2), and (g)(2), PDF pages 23-25
authorities.proposition: A discovery motion must attach or quote each disputed request and response and certify a good-faith effort to resolve the dispute. A discovery-motion response is due within fourteen days, and no reply is permitted unless ordered.

authorities.locator: Official May 2023 Local Civil Rules, Rule 26.1(a) and (d), PDF pages 42-44
authorities.proposition: Discovery materials ordinarily are not filed unless ordered or used in the proceeding. Discovery disputes receive the local expedited briefing schedule, including a fourteen-day response and no reply unless ordered.

authorities.locator: Official May 2023 Local Civil Rules, Rule 79.2, PDF pages 78-80
authorities.proposition: Sealing requires a court order. A filer must submit a public motion to seal and public docket notice addressing the governing standards; the proposed sealed document is provisionally sealed while the motion is resolved.

authorities.citation: E.D.N.C. Standing Order 25-SO-1, In re: Procedures for Access and Management of Sealed Documents (Sept. 24, 2025)
authorities.locator: In re: Procedures for Access and Management of Sealed Documents, Standing Order 25-SO-1, paragraphs 2-4 and supersession provision
authorities.proposition: Documents remain filed under Local Civil Rule 79.2 but sealed or restricted documents are not electronically accessible or viewable. CM/ECF cannot effect service, service must occur outside CM/ECF, entitled persons request paper copies from the clerk, and the order supersedes inconsistent local rules, orders, and manual provisions.
